0: The stone listens. We carved this warning at every threshold so the young would learn to walk softly.
A miner's tally: forty days without a tremor. The forty-first day is scratched out.
Resonant stone is quarried by song, not by pick. Strike it wrong and the whole seam answers.
Children's game: hum a note into the wall and count how long the mountain hums it back.
Whoever reads this has come down the old descent. Turn back, or learn to listen.
1: Surface shrine: offerings to the ridge, so the mist would hide the basins from outsiders.
The eastern door opens to one voice only, the voice the Key remembers.
Trade tally: salt and obsidian up from the coast, resonant stone sent down to it. Never the reverse.
A ridge-watcher's vow: no fires on the peaks, no songs above the treeline.
The basins were green once, before we drew the water down into the halls.
2: Water is the Vaelor's first servant. Weight is the second. Sound commands them both.
Counterweight masons were paid twice: once for the stone and once for its balance.
Flood-gate litany: open in the order of the river, close in the order of the sea.
An engineer's note: the channels sing when they run true. Silence means a blockage.
The shaft beneath this sanctuary was dug to listen to the deep, not to reach it.
3: Bridge-builders tuned each span so a marching column would never match its note.
One span was built wrong. They left it standing as a lesson and walked around it.
Fallen-stone prayer, worn smooth by hands: let the mountain take the stone, not the walker.
Surveyor's mark: below this point the rock is hollow for a thousand strides.
We built higher to hear further. The mountain heard us first.
4: Cave-farmers grew pale fungus in the dark galleries, watered by the condensation channels.
A sealed gallery: the air here hums at a pitch that makes the teeth ache. Keep it sealed.
Route mark in three scripts: Vaelor, coastal, and one nobody here can read.
The old survey party's chalk arrows run over Vaelor carvings that point the same way.
Listen at the cracks. Wind means a way out. A hum means turn back.
5: Aqueduct keepers lived in the walls, opening and closing sluices by the tone of the water.
Toll stone: water was taxed by the measure, sound by the hour.
Graffiti from a keeper's niche: my brother tends the Heart now. He no longer sleeps.
The temple sank on purpose. We drowned it to quiet it.
Above the keepers' doors: the water carries what the stone remembers.
6: The drowned temple was the tuning-house of the kingdom. Every node was first sung here.
Divers' slate, Vaelor style: hold a breath for each verse of the descent hymn.
The great wheel turns the city's water. Stop the wheel and the lower halls flood within a day.
The priest-engineers flooded this hall when the tuning began to drift. It never stopped drifting.
Inscription on a fallen statue: we were not punished. We were simply heard.
7: Scholar's index: four nodes, one Heart. Never sing to all four at once.
City census, last entry: the eastern quarter has been evacuated for the third time this year.
Market rule: no bells, no drums, no singing in the plaza during the turning.
A teacher's tablet: the Heart does not create the hum. It only makes it louder.
Final decree: seal the Vault, silence the nodes, and leave the city to the mist.
8: A traitor's tablet from the old kingdom: one who sold the Key's song to the coast. His name is chiselled out.
A healers' guild sign: rest, water and silence for those who heard the Voice Below.
Two sets of footprints carved into a doorstep: those who stayed and those who left.
Vaelor proverb: a door opened for gold does not close for regret.
The guard post's last log: they came with the Key, and we let them pass.
9: Heart Road milestone: the closer you walk, the quieter you speak.
Pilgrims left their voices here: a stone for every word they would not say in the Vault.
The conduits under the road carry the hum to the nodes. Crack them and the road sings.
A road-warden's warning: blasting powder is the loudest prayer. The mountain always answers it.
We built the road straight so the hum could run along it. Nothing that straight survives a quake.
10: The Heart Vault is a stone throat. It does not think. It only answers.
Node keepers wore wax in their ears and read the stone by touch.
To quiet the Vault, silence the nodes from the outside in: water, weight, position, song.
Whoever controls all four nodes can make the mountain speak, once.
Last Vaelor words in the Vault: it worked, until it didn't.
11: Escape tunnel carving: the way out is always uphill and always toward the wind.
The Vaelor did not die here. They walked out, and the mist forgot them.
Daylight shaft blessing: may the stone forget your footsteps.
A child's handprint in resonant stone, still faintly humming.
The mountain is quiet now. Let it stay that way.
